I read the sequence as the concatenation of the decimal representations of the integers, where each integer $n$ is written $n$ times. This matches the given start "122333444455555…", and it is the only reading under which "digits" makes sense once $n \ge 10$.

**Block lengths.** The 1-digit blocks ($n=1,\dots,9$) have total length $\sum_{n=1}^{9} n = 45$. For $n \ge 10$, block $n$ has length $2n$. So the total length through block $k$ (for $k \ge 9$) is

$$L(k) = 45 + \sum_{n=10}^{k} 2n = k(k+1) - 45.$$

**Locating position 4501.** We need $L(k) \ge 4501$, i.e. $k(k+1) \ge 4546$.
- $L(66) = 66\cdot 67 - 45 = 4377$
- $L(67) = 67\cdot 68 - 45 = 4511$

So position 4501 lies in block 67, at offset $4501 - 4377 = 124$. Block 67 is "67" repeated 67 times, so its digits alternate 6, 7, 6, 7, … Position 124 is even, so the digit is **7**.

**Locating position 4052.**
- $L(63) = 63\cdot 64 - 45 = 3987$
- $L(64) = 64\cdot 65 - 45 = 4115$

So position 4052 lies in block 64, at offset $4052 - 3987 = 65$. Block 64 is "64" repeated 64 times, so its digits alternate 6, 4, 6, 4, … Position 65 is odd, so the digit is **6**.

**Sum:** $7 + 6 = 13$.

ANSWER: 13
